tagline: The world's largest independent, pure-play provider of aerospace engine aftermarket services for fixed and rotary wing aircraft
hero_kpi_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA is selected as the primary KPI because it reflects the company's underlying operating performance and is used by management and creditors to assess financial health and covenant compliance.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Adjusted operating profit that excludes non-recurring items such as depreciation or share-based charges.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA increases due to improved operational efficiency and higher activity volumes.

kpis.name: Net Cash from Operations
kpis.explanation: Cash generated from the company's core business activities.
kpis.description: Net cash from operations surges in 2025, driven by improved working capital management and a strong increase in net income.

kpis.name: Capex
kpis.explanation: Expenditures to acquire or upgrade equipment, buildings, or technology.
kpis.description: Capex declines in 2025 following a peak in 2024 related to the LEAP program rollout and the acquisition of Aero Turbine.
kpis.signal: Reduction in investments following LEAP program deployment

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total sales generated by the company.
kpis.description: Approximately 80% of revenue comes from long-term contracts, ensuring high visibility.
kpis.signal: Sustained growth driven by long-term contracts

kpis.name: Long-term Agreement Revenue Share
kpis.explanation: Percentage of sales tied to multi-year contracts.
kpis.description: The majority of revenue is secured by long-term agreements, reducing volatility.

kpis.name: Long-Term Debt Repayment
kpis.description: After a peak in 2024 related to post-IPO debt restructuring, repayments decrease in 2025.
kpis.signal: Marked reduction in financial leverage post-IPO

kpis.name: Depreciation & Amortization
kpis.explanation: Allocation of asset costs over their useful life.
kpis.description: Depreciation and amortization increase slightly, reflecting continued investment in assets.

risks.title: Costs and resources associated with being a public company
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned at the beginning of the 'Risks Related to Management and Employees' section. The language is direct but does not exhibit extreme intensity. The risk is intrinsic to public company status, therefore stable but ongoing.

risks.title: Reliance on non-GAAP financial measures
risks.score_rationale: Described in detail in the 'Key Performance Indicators and Non-GAAP Financial Measures' section. The language is descriptive and highlights limitations and comparability concerns. This risk relates to financial reporting and investor perception.

risks.title: Costs and complexity of acquisitions
risks.score_rationale: Acquisition costs are mentioned in the reconciliation table and in the results discussion. The 2024 acquisition of Aero Turbine for $114.1M is explicitly cited as a source of costs and increased intangible assets. The language is factual but the impact is significant.

risks.title: Rising material and labor costs
risks.score_rationale: The 'Cost of revenue' section details cost increases due to volume, materials, and direct labor. The language is descriptive but the impact on gross margin is direct.

risks.title: Risks related to business transformation and expansion
risks.score_rationale: Business transformation costs (LEAP, CFM) are listed in the EBITDA reconciliation. Expansion of CFM56 capacity is mentioned. The language is factual regarding incurred expenses.

ai_positioning.summary: SARO does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K filing. There is no indication of AI use or development in its operations.
